Notes: ROUND AN - PIXELLAB: the village football ground seen from above - stands, beer tents, the maypole, village roofs and trees around the pitch (art_source/pixellab/stadium/stadium_back.png, 688 x 384, stretched to 3840 x 2160; the pitch covers the middle two-thirds). Layered file: art_source/aseprite/stadium.aseprite. THE STADIUM BEHIND THE PITCH. Draw it 3840 x 2160 - 16:9 at 4K, half again bigger than the pitch so there is something to see when the camera moves. It sits BEHIND the grass and it is the only layer that moves at a different speed: Parallax 0.25 means it drifts a quarter as fast as the camera, which is what reads as distance. It is only visible round the edges of the pitch and through anything transparent you draw in the pitch image, so put the stands and the sky in the top and bottom thirds. Put the file in assets/field/ as stadium_back.png. Leave Image blank and there is no background, which is how the game looks today

THE PLAYING SURFACE, AND THE ONE NUMBER YOU ASKED FOR. Draw it 2560 x 1440. IT HAS TO BE 16:9 - the camera's widest shot COVERS the pitch rather than fitting inside it, so anything taller than the window is cropped top and bottom and anything wider is cropped at the sides. 2560 x 1440 is the window's shape, sharp at 1080p and at 1440p. THE WHITE LINES DO NOT GO TO THE EDGE. A real pitch is 1.54:1 and a window is 1.78:1, so draw the lines inside a margin and fill the rest with grass, a running track, whatever you like. The margin is pitch_inset_x (6%) and pitch_inset_y (10%) in Tuning.csv, which at this size means THE LINES OCCUPY THE MIDDLE 2253 x 1152 PIXELS, centred. Everything in the match is measured against that inner rectangle. The file is stretched to exactly Width x Height whatever size you draw it, so you can work at 5120 x 2880 and it still lands correctly. Put it in assets/field/

AN OVERLAY ON TOP OF EVERYTHING, for the Stadium screen to unlock later. Tint is multiplied over the layer, so a warm colour here is floodlights and a cold one is a night game. Requires works the same way it does everywhere else - blank means always on, and a row whose Requires fails is simply not drawn. No Image means this row does nothing yet

A SECOND BACKGROUND LAYER, drawn between the stadium and the grass. For a crowd you unlock, or banners, or a stand that fills up as you win. Same size as the background
